```{python}
import sys

from shared.components import (
    chart_card,
    method_and_sources,
    prev_next,
    related_studies,
    stat_tile,
    stat_tiles,
)
from shared.context import load_context
from shared.glossary import glossary_popovers
from shared.outputs import read_output
from shared.paths import CASE_STUDIES, REPO_URL, ROOT

STUDY = CASE_STUDIES / "06_livestock_supply"
sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDY / "analysis"))
import figures as F  # noqa: E402

data, prov_data, notes_data = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "livestock_supply.csv")
check, prov_check, notes_check = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "chicken_slaughter_check.csv")
rev, prov_rev, notes_rev = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "edition_revisions.csv")
ctx = load_context(STUDY / "context.yml")  # studies and reports, background only (policy §7)

v = data.set_index(["product", "year"])
LAST = int(data.year.max())
C0, E0 = int(data[data["product"] == "chicken"].year.min()), int(data[data["product"] == "eggs"].year.min())
B0 = int(data[data["product"] == "beef"].year.min())
A = 2010  # comparison year for the chain chart


def share(p, y=LAST):
    return v.loc[(p, y), "local_share_pct"]


def pct(x):
    return f"{x:.0f}%" if x >= 10 else f"{x:.1f}%"


def num(x):
    return f"{x:,.0f}"


chick = data[data["product"] == "chicken"].set_index("year")
first_90 = int(chick[chick.local_share_pct >= 90].index.min())
low_after = int(chick.loc[first_90:LAST - 1, "local_share_pct"].idxmin())
imp_prev, imp_last = chick.loc[LAST - 1, "imports"], chick.loc[LAST, "imports"]
loc_prev, loc_last = chick.loc[LAST - 1, "local"], chick.loc[LAST, "local"]
eggs = data[data["product"] == "eggs"].set_index("year")
egg_min = eggs.local_share_pct.min()
beef = data[data["product"] == "beef"].set_index("year")
beef_total = beef.local + beef.imports
cf_first = int(beef[beef.imports_chilled_frozen > 0].index.min())
kg = check.kg_per_bird.round(3).unique()
band = chick.loc[first_90 : LAST - 1, "local_share_pct"]
beef_max = beef.local_share_pct.max()
# Stated in the text below; stop the build rather than publish them if the data changes.
assert share("chicks") < share("chicks", A) and share("hatching_eggs") < share("hatching_eggs", A)
assert len(kg) == 1, "Chicken tonnes no longer use one weight per bird."
```

::: {.study-intro}
This case study looks at **how much of Brunei's chicken, eggs and beef was produced in the
country**, using the Agriculture and Agrifood Department's yearly figures for local production
and imports from 1992 to 2020. It also follows chicken back through its supply chain, to the
chicks and the eggs they hatch from. The data ends in 2020, although it was published in 2025.
It shows **what changed, not why**.

It asks two questions, answered in the conclusion:

1. **How much of Brunei's chicken, eggs and beef was produced locally from 1992 to 2020?**
2. **How local is the chicken supply chain, from hatching eggs to meat?**
:::

```{python}
stat_tiles(
    stat_tile(f"Chicken meat produced locally, {LAST}", pct(share("chicken")), "", f"of supply ({C0}: {pct(share('chicken', C0))})"),
    stat_tile(f"Eggs produced locally, {LAST}", pct(share("eggs")), "", f"of supply (never below {pct(egg_min)} since {E0})"),
    stat_tile(f"Beef produced locally, {LAST}", pct(share("beef")), "", f"of supply ({B0}: {pct(share('beef', B0))})"),
)
```

```{python}
fig, table = F.shares(data)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Chicken went from about a third local to almost all local; eggs stayed local; beef stayed imported",
    subtitle=f"Local share of supply: local production ÷ (local production + imports), % · {C0}–{LAST} (beef from {B0})",
    alt=(
        f"Three area charts. Chicken meat rises from {pct(share('chicken', C0))} local in {C0} to "
        f"over 90% from {first_90}, ending at {pct(share('chicken'))} in {LAST}. Eggs stay close "
        f"to 100% throughout. Beef never goes above {pct(beef_max)} and is {pct(share('beef'))} in {LAST}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_data,
    table=table,
    height=300,
    mobile_fig=F.shares(data, cols=1)[0],
    mobile_height=760,
)
```

## Chicken meat, 1992–2020

In `{python} C0`, about `{python} pct(share("chicken", C0))` of the chicken meat in Brunei
was produced locally. Local production then grew quickly, and the
[local share of supply]{.term term="local-share-of-supply"} passed 90% in
`{python} first_90`. It stayed between `{python} pct(band.min())` and `{python} pct(band.max())`
until `{python} LAST - 1`, with its lowest point in `{python} low_after`.

**In `{python} LAST`, imports fell from `{python} num(imp_prev)` to `{python} num(imp_last)`
tonnes while local production rose to `{python} num(loc_last)` tonnes**, so the local share
reached `{python} pct(share("chicken"))`.

```{python}
fig, table = F.chicken_volumes(data)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Local chicken production grew {loc_last / chick.loc[C0, 'local']:.1f}× while imports shrank",
    subtitle=f"Chicken meat supply, thousand tonnes · {C0}–{LAST} · teal: produced locally · grey: imported",
    alt=(
        f"Stacked bar chart. In {C0}, {num(chick.loc[C0, 'local'])} t were produced locally and "
        f"{num(chick.loc[C0, 'imports'])} t imported. By {LAST}, {num(loc_last)} t were local "
        f"and {num(imp_last)} t imported."
    ),
    provenance=prov_data,
    table=table,
)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="How local chicken is measured"}
**The Department's local chicken figures are calculated from the number of birds slaughtered,
at `{python} f"{kg[0]:g}"` kg per bird.** In every year from 2011 to `{python} LAST`, the
tonnes equal the birds slaughtered × `{python} f"{kg[0]:g}"` kg exactly, so they are an estimate
rather than a weighed total. This measure is not the official
[self-sufficiency ratio]{.term term="self-sufficiency-ratio"}, which also subtracts exports and
can go above 100%.
:::

## The chicken supply chain, 2010 and 2020

Broiler farms raise [day-old chicks]{.term term="day-old-chick"}, which hatch from
[fertilized (hatching) eggs]{.term term="hatching-egg"}. The further back along this chain,
the more of the supply was imported. In `{python} LAST`, `{python} pct(share("chicken"))` of
chicken meat was local, against `{python} pct(share("chicks"))` of day-old chicks and
`{python} pct(share("hatching_eggs"))` of hatching eggs.

```{python}
fig, table = F.chain(data, A, LAST)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Only {pct(share('hatching_eggs'))} of hatching eggs were local in {LAST}, against {pct(share('chicken'))} of chicken meat",
    subtitle=f"Local share of supply at each step of the chicken chain, % · {A} and {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Bar chart. Hatching eggs: {pct(share('hatching_eggs', A))} local in {A}, "
        f"{pct(share('hatching_eggs'))} in {LAST}. Day-old chicks: {pct(share('chicks', A))}, then "
        f"{pct(share('chicks'))}. Chicken meat: {pct(share('chicken', A))}, then {pct(share('chicken'))}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_data,
    table=table,
    height=300,
)
```

Between `{python} A` and `{python} LAST`, the local share of day-old chicks fell from
`{python} pct(share("chicks", A))` to `{python} pct(share("chicks"))`, and of hatching eggs from
`{python} pct(share("hatching_eggs", A))` to `{python} pct(share("hatching_eggs"))`, while
chicken meat rose.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="What was reported in studies"}
These come from published studies and reports, not from the data above.

- **Which farms competed best.** A study of Brunei's livestock industry found it was heavily
  protected, and that only very large farms producing poultry meat and eggs had a comparative
  advantage; beef cattle did not, despite protection (`{python} ctx["mohamed2004"].cite()`).
- **Before and during COVID-19.** Researchers at Universiti Brunei Darussalam reported that
  before the pandemic, poultry met close to 100% of local demand for eggs and chicken, but that
  there were shortages of chicken and other meat during it, linked to higher demand and the
  cost of logistics and feed (`{python} ctx["musa2021"].cite()`).
- **An earlier claim.** Officials described poultry and eggs as nearly self-sufficient since
  1994 (`{python} ctx["searca2016"].cite()`). In the Department's own figures this holds for
  eggs; for chicken meat, the local share passed 90% only in `{python} first_90`.
- **Since `{python} LAST`.** A 2026 regional report put Brunei's self-sufficiency ratios for
  chicken meat and eggs above 100%, with beef substantially lower
  (`{python} ctx["khut2026"].cite()`).

**None of these explains the year-to-year changes in the data above.** The 2026 report uses a
self-sufficiency ratio, which is measured differently from the local share used here.
:::

## Eggs and beef, 1992–2020

**Eggs were almost entirely local throughout**: the local share never fell below
`{python} pct(egg_min)`, and production grew from `{python} f"{eggs.loc[E0, 'local']:.0f}"`
million eggs in `{python} E0` to `{python} f"{eggs.loc[LAST, 'local']:.0f}"` million in
`{python} LAST`.

**Beef was mostly imported.** Local production was `{python} num(beef.loc[LAST, "local"])`
tonnes in `{python} LAST`, `{python} pct(share("beef"))` of a supply of
`{python} num(beef_total[LAST])` tonnes. Imports came as live animals, slaughtered in Brunei,
and, from `{python} cf_first`, as chilled and frozen beef, which was the larger of the two in
most years since.

```{python}
fig, table = F.beef_volumes(data)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Local beef was a sliver of supply in every year from {B0} to {LAST}",
    subtitle=f"Beef supply by source, tonnes · {B0}–{LAST} · teal: produced locally · chilled & frozen imports first recorded in {cf_first}",
    alt=(
        f"Stacked bar chart of beef supply. Live imports make up most of it in the early 2000s; "
        f"chilled and frozen imports appear from {cf_first} and grow. Local production is a thin "
        f"band, {num(beef.loc[LAST, 'local'])} t in {LAST}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_data,
    table=table,
)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="What was reported about beef"}
A historical study describes Brunei's beef production today as **importing live animals and
slaughtering them in domestic halal-certified abattoirs** (`{python} ctx["takami2023"].cite()`).
That fits the large "imported live" share above: those animals are slaughtered in Brunei but
counted as imports, not local production.
:::

## Conclusion

- **How much of Brunei's chicken, eggs and beef was produced locally from 1992 to 2020?**
  Chicken meat went from about `{python} pct(share("chicken", C0))` local in `{python} C0` to
  `{python} pct(share("chicken"))` in `{python} LAST`, passing 90% in `{python} first_90`. Eggs
  stayed almost entirely local. Beef stayed mostly imported: `{python} pct(share("beef"))` local
  in `{python} LAST`.
- **How local is the chicken supply chain, from hatching eggs to meat?** Less local the further
  back it goes: in `{python} LAST`, `{python} pct(share("chicken"))` of chicken meat,
  `{python} pct(share("chicks"))` of day-old chicks and `{python} pct(share("hatching_eggs"))`
  of hatching eggs were local, and the earlier steps became less local after `{python} A`.

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" title="What this doesn't tell us"}
<!-- Side note: required on every case study (DESIGN.md §4.1). -->
- **Why.** The data doesn't explain the changes, including the drop in chicken imports
  in `{python} LAST`.
- **Exports and stocks.** No export or stock figures are published, so the local share is not a
  full self-sufficiency ratio.
- **Exact chicken weights.** Local chicken tonnes are estimated at `{python} f"{kg[0]:g}"` kg
  per bird.
- **Other inputs.** Feed, medicines and breeding stock aren't covered.
- **Beef before `{python} cf_first`.** Chilled and frozen beef imports are 0 until
  `{python} cf_first`, probably because they weren't recorded, so earlier local shares may be
  too high.
- **After `{python} LAST`.** The Department's tables end in `{python} LAST`.
:::
